# Can the product's page server read the new system's library? Not as it is stored (2026-11-16, $0)

**Answer: no. The existing page server, given the new system's stored week (a copy of
`poc/data/clean-lean-week-2026-11-14/week-r2/c1/judge/draw-c1/views.sqlite`), returns an empty library: `/library` → `"views": []`,
`/views?object=NVDA` → `[]`, `/views/v1` → not found, `/days` → no first or last day. Only `/views/v1/history` answers (the
judgements of one question).**

**Why (read in the code):** the product's read side places every question in time through the record of completed days
(`src/hivemind/views/store.py`, `day_start_seq`: "the seq of the last completed day before it, or 0 before the first completed
day"; `bundle.py` lists days from `days_completed`). The new system's store, written by the judging adapter, holds no completed
day (`days_completed`: 0 rows), so every question sits after the cut-off and is hidden.

**What it means:** gate 5 of `NEW-SYSTEM-FRAME.md` (integration with production storage and the pages) is not started, and this
is its first concrete defect: the adapter writes the questions and judgements but not the days. The fix belongs to the writer
(AGENTS §3, one owner: where the data is written). Not changed now: a run is live and no package code is edited while it
runs; and integration is not this step's work (D563). Recorded as an open defect for the integration step.

Server started on port 8791 for this check and stopped after it; the store was a copy.


## The cause, corrected, and the fix (2026-11-16, $0)

**The first diagnosis was incomplete.** On a copy of the fortnight's store, recording the completed days alone made `/days` answer
but left the library empty. The page maps every sequence number to a day through the processing record
(`src/hivemind/service.py`, `seq_day_map`: "sequence number → the publication day of the item or daily round written under it",
read from `processing_steps`), which the new system's store does not hold either (0 rows). With both recorded on the copy (one
processing step per article, its sequence and day; one completed day per day, its last sequence), the page lists all 12 judged
questions with their present answers and details.

**The fix, at the writer** (`clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/stage_b/ladder_adapter.py`, the judge step of the live clean path):
`LadderAdapter.record_article` writes the article's processing step (`store.mark_step`, step `handed_over`, the day as its time
field: no clock) before its records; `LadderAdapter.complete_day` writes the day's end (`store.complete_day`) after its round of
judgements. Neither table is read by the judging code or either adapter (searched). The base adapter
(`clean-arch/e2e-2026-11-09/adapter.py`) is frozen with the unseeded measurement (`clean-arch/unseeded-2026-11-10/unseeded-frozen.sha256`;
the runner refuses to start when it changes, which is how the first attempt to put the methods there was caught); it is
unchanged, and its own day loop, which only that measurement's harness uses, does not record them.

**Proved:**
- a test (`test_ladder_adapter.py::test_the_page_can_place_every_judged_view_in_time`): every completed article has its step at its
  own sequence and day, every day its end at its last sequence, and the page's own listing (`service.views`) shows every judged
  view; 28 of 28 tests of the file pass; two mutants on a scratch mirror (no completed day; no processing step) each fail it;
- the extension proof re-run with the change (`extension_proof.py`): 19 of 19, every judge request and every judgement equal to
  the stored week's; the draw it writes holds 235 steps and 7 days, and the page lists its 7 judged questions.

Not yet: the stores already written (the fortnight's draw and earlier ones) do not hold the records; a page over them needs the
draw re-run, or a separate back-fill that would be its own change. Integration as a whole (gate 5) is more than this: the page
was built for the old system's questions and has not been read by anyone over the new system's.

**The answer-choice reading confirms a failure on this draw; it does not prove that a carried library cannot improve the gate.** The page change also needs one more check before it is recorded as a completed fix: the new processing records have readers beyond the page.

For example, both favourable and unfavourable readings miss lines 1, 2, 3 and 5; line 4 is met, and line 6 is **not measured**. The counts are 7 or 5 of 13 topics right, including 6 or 4 by written choices. Those are scaled diagnostic counts, not Alex’s original 44-topic acceptance. [Stage A report](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/data/clean-carried-run-2026-11-16/stage-a/report.txt)

The claim that the starting condition “was not the reason” goes too far. This draw started its second week with a library and still failed several lines. The October and July readings used different articles, topics and draws, so they do not isolate the effect of the starting library. The system also declined **one topic in all three attempts**; the readers agreed that those refusals were justified under the theme rule. [Stage A report](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/data/clean-carried-run-2026-11-16/stage-a/report.txt), [October result](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/second-week/RESULT.md)

On the proposed faults:

- **Due date:** both third readers uphold the Rubin annual-report concern in two attempts. The CPO due-date findings remain **unresolved between the third readers**; they appear upheld only when unresolved points count against the answer. A date before the named report creates a real risk, but “the judge would close still open where the event happened” is not yet shown. The clean replay stops when an open question reaches its due day; the closing PRD says pull mode freezes its last judgement. Neither establishes the actual eventual outcome in these cases. [Stage A report](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/data/clean-carried-run-2026-11-16/stage-a/report.txt), [closing PRD](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/prd/07-final-verdict.md:9)
- **Reference:** seven of 36 written answers have `XR` marks against them in the report. Their product effect needs tracing: the design says an **event’s reference field is not shown to the judge**, which forms its own reference from the evidence. An empty field can still mislead a page reader, but fixing it is not yet shown to change a judgement. D411 specifically governs a *figure’s* last-reported amount and range; the expectation rule for events also comes from the broader reference contract. [Stage A report](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/data/clean-carried-run-2026-11-16/stage-a/report.txt), [reference contract](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/DESIGN.md:794), [D411](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:4530)
- The MIIT **“and” versus “or”** concern is serious. The third readers disagree about how to count it under the additional named-fault mark, so preserve that dispute rather than presenting all three as unanimously upheld named faults. [Stage A report](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/data/clean-carried-run-2026-11-16/stage-a/report.txt)

The page work has evidence behind it: the writer now records articles and completed days, and the test checks that the page’s listing includes every judged view. I independently confirmed that the frozen base adapter matches its recorded hash. I did **not** rerun the tests in this read-only review, and the saved `proof-output.txt` predates the adapter change, so that file alone does not verify the claimed post-change 19/19 replay or 287-test result. [Writer](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/stage_b/ladder_adapter.py:234), [test](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/stage_b/test_ladder_adapter.py:104), [integration record](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/carried-run/INTEGRATION-CHECK.md)

There is a material scope issue before calling C behaviour-neutral. The writer records each article as `handed_over: ok` **before the day’s judging round**. That field is also read by production dispatch and recovery: `is_processed` can cause an article to be skipped, and the last step controls resumption. The successful replay is useful evidence that stored judgements stayed the same on that path; it does not establish crash, failed-judgement or later-reader behaviour. [Writer loop](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/stage_b/ladder_adapter.py:319), [dispatch](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/src/hivemind/dispatch.py:25), [processing records](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/src/hivemind/views/store.py:440)

**My recommended next iteration is the $0 due-date census, with the page fix’s reader and failure-state audit completed in the same slice.** Count distinct questions and attempts separately; trace each proposed early deadline through the named settling material, the actual judge request, and the closing path. Include counterexamples where an event can be established before a later report, and report potential wrong closures separately from demonstrated wrong closures. In parallel conceptually, but without concurrent edits to shared code, check every reader of the new day and processing records, including a judge failure after article records are committed.

Keep the page change as an **unaccepted candidate** until those checks and the post-change replay evidence are recorded. D439 authorizes the council to decide the next bounded version while Alex is inactive; it does not authorize changing Alex’s underlying D403 rule or the frozen ruler. The question about the six lines remains for Alex **after Deck 1**, as D560 says. If the census shows that a repair requires changing D403, bring that precise conflict and its evidence to him rather than assuming the new version may override it. [D403](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:4414), [D439](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:4871), [D560](/Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/DECISIONS-log.md:7047)

CONSENSUS: no, because the page change’s non-display readers and failure states remain unverified, and the current evidence does not establish the claimed causal effect of the carried library or the due dates.
